counterfactual_missing_items: Trichography: Showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end
Eyebrow hairs were sparse and less than 5 mm long
scalp hairs were coarse and brittle
decisive_items: The condition had progressively worsened to involve 90% of her body surface area (BSA).
response.rationale: R2 best accounts for the psoriasiform spongiotic biopsy and the widespread serpiginous erythematous plaques/erythroderma, fitting PRP better than psoriasis. R1 is weakened by spongiosis and the non-psoriatic double-edged scale/trichorrhexis invaginata. R4 only captures hair findings. The trichography finding strongly suggests Netherton syndrome, so R2 is only a default champion among the supplied candidates.

rejected.why: Alopecia is a sign rather than a diagnosis; it ignores the widespread skin plaques, biopsy, and trichography.
